adjudication.rule: Predeclared in the procedure, Step 0, before any observation: 'A PASS recorded against a build that lacks the fix certifies nothing. If you are unsure which build is live, say so and I will treat the result as NOT_ESTABLISHED rather than PASS.'

F065_PB11_LIVE_CERTIFICATION.basis: BUILD ATTRIBUTION ONLY — not a failure, and not a doubt about the observations.
F065_PB11_LIVE_CERTIFICATION.whyThisMatters: F065's recorded implementation state is 'structural fix PUSHED' — pushed, not confirmed deployed — and the Part-1/Part-2 refinements are committed locally and are certainly not deployed. Certification attaches to an artifact. Without knowing which artifact was exercised, a PASS records that some build behaved correctly, which cannot be carried forward as certification of this one.
F065_PB11_LIVE_CERTIFICATION.whatWasNonethelessObserved: A1, A2 and A3 all report PASS with concrete detail, and A2 reports the proof-critical elements: a NON-PASSWORD establishment path (institution sign-in), no /login at any point, and the session surviving the reload. That is exactly the behaviour F065 predicts. It is held as OBSERVED, not as CERTIFIED.

S2_S3_SIGNED_OUT_PROBE.note: Every B step matched its predeclared expectation, including the two counter-checks that make the set meaningful rather than self-confirming: B4 (/admin refuses unauthenticated entry — PD-1 scope exclusion is not a security bypass) and B5 (/public still renders — the fail-closed contract has not over-closed and broken acquisition). B1 reports the exact preserved destination string.
S2_S3_SIGNED_OUT_PROBE.strength: B1-B6 are self-describing observations of live behaviour and stand on their own as evidence that the live site currently enforces fail-closed routing with destination preservation.
